doc.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2024 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Phrasing and rhythm make the right notes
summary: Rowe asks if rhythm justifies notes; McPherson says the right phrase makes the note right, a package deal.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: If the when is working well for you, does that help to — I’m going to use the word “justify” pitches that maybe you didn’t mean to play but if rhythmically they fit into your phrasing, does that sort of —

Well I think — here’s what I think — I think there’s something magic about concerning yourself with the phrasing and the rhythmic aspect. And what I mean by that I think once you start thinking that way there is something very compelling about that because you’ve trained your mind to actually think that way, and that has a way of setting up a part of © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

your mind for it to actually be freed up and I think you start playing the right notes. Yeah. Because there’s something compelling and hypnotic about that. For me. I can see — there’s a high tendency of the note being right because some kind of way because the phrase rhythmically is the right configuration for the moment. It is so much the truth that the truth of the note will be there with that, it’s a package deal.
I like that. It’s a package deal.
